prerequisites: Kinematics of particles and rigid bodies
Dynamics of a particle and rigid body

learning_outcomes.text: Have knowledge and understanding of linear differential equations applicable to mechanical vibration problems.
Have knowledge and understanding of the fundamentals of mechanical vibrations.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve mechanical vibration problems using established methods.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve mechanical vibration problems.
Have an understanding of applicable methods and techniques in mechanical vibrations and their limitations.
Knowledge and understanding of the scientific and mathematical principles underlying their branch of engineering.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their branch of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
The understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in an area of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects implying knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.

syllabus_topics: Solution of first-order homogeneous differential equations
Solution of first-order non-homogeneous linear differential equations
Numerical methods for solving differential equations
Solution of differential equations using MATLAB
Solution of differential equations using SIMULINK
Energy of a Simple Harmonic Motion
Damped mechanical vibrations and forced vibrations
Solution to the differential equation of damped motion
Systems with 2 Degrees of Freedom and N Degrees of Freedom
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a 50% final exam and 50% continuous assessment (10% laboratory practices, 20% weekly exercises, 20% midterm exam). A minimum of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in the final exam to be averaged with continuous assessment. Attendance to laboratory practices is mandatory to pass the course in the ordinary session. In the extraordinary session, the exam can be 100% of the grade or combined with continuous assessment if followed, with a minimum of 4 points required for weighting.
